parsed.response: Do not let token evidence introduce renderer or component package work. Treat the candidate as a refund review workbench boundary slice with acceptable primitive, state, static, browser, and accessibility coverage, but reject the visual-token evidence expectations that claim a component package is ready or that a renderer package can drive the default component library. The next agent should scope token evidence to the active design-system source: color, type, spacing, status and decision roles, import-boundary compliance, semantic fallback, forced-colors behavior, and non-text contrast. Any renderer or component-package claim needs a separate package-readiness review with explicit contracts, exports, integration tests, and ownership.
parsed.handoff: Design-system owner: remove renderer/component-package readiness claims because adapter token evidence only proves boundary styling and provenance; add separate package contracts and tests before authorizing renderer or component work.
parsed.rationale: The evidence supports the refund review workbench boundary and its accessibility checks, but the visual token adapter is not authority for renderer behavior or component-package readiness. Color, type, spacing tokens and semantic roles can validate token use in this slice; they cannot create default component library behavior or expand the active boundary.
